### Part 1

#### 1. Create a new RStudio Project and name it `hw_9`

#### 2. Within that project, create a new Quarto document and modify the YAML to:

#### 3. Your first code chunk should:

-   Be labelled `load-packages`
-   Load all the necessary packages (please don't load packages you do **not** use)
-   Include options for this code chunk so it will not display the code or the results from the code

#### 4. Your second code chunk should:

-   Be labelled `load-data`
-   Import the following three data sets, each as separate objects
    + `hw8_ids.xlsx`
    + `year1_score.csv`
    + `year1_demo.xlsx`
    + `year2_score.csv`
    + `year2_demo.xlsx`
-   Recreate the data object from Homework 8 named `year12`. Use your code from Homework 8, but try to create the data with one conitnuous pipeline.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

hw8_ids <- read_csv(here::here("data", "hw8_ids.csv"))
year1_score <- read_csv(here::here("data", "year1_score.csv"))
year2_score <- read_csv(here::here("data", "year2_score.csv"))
year1_demo <- import(here::here("data", "year1_demo.xlsx")) |> 
  as_tibble()
year2_demo <- import(here::here("data", "year2_demo.xlsx")) |> 
  as_tibble()

year12 <- hw8_ids |> 
  filter(id != 51) |> 
  left_join(
    year1_score |>
      filter(!is.na(id_student)) |> 
      arrange(id_student, desc(date)) |> 
      group_by(id_student) |> 
      mutate(n = row_number()) |> 
      filter(n == 1) |> 
      select(-n),
    join_by(id == id_student)
  ) |> 
  left_join(year1_demo) |> 
  left_join(
    year2_score |> 
      filter(!is.na(id_student)),
    suffix = c("_year1", "_year2"),
    join_by(id == id_student)
  ) |> 
  left_join(
    year2_demo |> 
      rename(frl = FRL),
    suffix = c("_year1", "_year2"),
    join_by(id)
  )
  
  
```


#### 5. Describe why the combined data set is not tidy.

<!-- There is information in the column headings, namely year (1, 2). -->

#### 6. Your third code chunk should:

-   Have a meaningful label (do not use spaces or capital letters or underscores)
-   Tidy the combined data set
-   Save the tidy data to the data folder in your project as `year12_tidy`

```{r}
#| label: tidy-data

year12_tidy <- year12 %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(id, name),
    names_to = c("names", "year"),
    names_sep = "_",
    values_to = "values",
    values_transform = list(values = as.character)
  ) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = names,
    values_from = values
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    year = parse_number(year),
    score = as.numeric(score),
    date = as.Date(date),
    across(c(sex:frl), ~str_to_lower(.))
  )



# export(year12_tidy, here("data", "year12_tidy.csv"))
```

#### 7. Your fourth code chunk should include code that:

-   Computes the *n* (how many students), min, max, *SD*, and mean of the *score* by *frl* and *year*
-   Show these results in a table **and** a figure. You can chose to display any/all stats that you like in the figure.

```{r}
#| label: stat-info
#| output: false

d_summary <- year12_tidy %>% 
  group_by(year, frl) %>% 
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    min = min(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) 
```

```{r}
#| label: stat-tbl
#| tbl-cap: Descriptive statistics for score by FRL status and year
#| results: asis
#| output: false

d_summary %>% 
  kable(digits = 1,
         col.names = c("Year", "FRL", "n", "Min", "Max", "SD", "Mean")) %>% 
  kable_styling(latex_options = "striped", full_width = FALSE) |> 
  add_header_above(c(" " = 3, "Score" = 4))
```

```{r}
#| label: stat-fig
#| fig-cap: Descriptive statistics for score by FRL status and year
#| output: false

d_summary %>% 
  ungroup() |> 
  ggplot(aes(as.factor(year), mean, color = frl, group = frl)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(y = "Average Score",
       x = "Year",
       title = "Score Results",
       subtitle = "Mean Score by FRL Status and Year",
       color = "FRL")
```

#### 8. Ok, let's try to place this in the context of "the real world." Did you notice that the *n* bounced around a bit in your previous table? That is because students' demographic info can change across years 😮! You are going to create a data set that will work for a linear mixed-effect model (don't worry if this doesn't mean anything to you). Basically, each student ID should have two rows: one for the year 1 score and one for the year 2 score. But their demographic info (i.e., sex, el, and frl) should not change. Name the object `lme_year12`. Describe what you decided to do and why.


```{r}
#| label: lme-data

# I just decided to keep the demographic info from Year 1. So I reran the join code, but dropped the jon for year2_demo.

lme_year12 <- hw8_ids |> 
  filter(id != 51) |> 
  left_join(
    year1_score |>
      filter(!is.na(id_student)) |> 
      arrange(id_student, desc(date)) |> 
      group_by(id_student) |> 
      mutate(n = row_number()) |> 
      filter(n == 1) |> 
      select(-n),
    join_by(id == id_student)
  ) |> 
  left_join(year1_demo) |> 
  left_join(
    year2_score |> 
      filter(!is.na(id_student)),
    suffix = c("_year1", "_year2"),
    join_by(id == id_student)
  ) |> # the code up to here is just pasted from my load-data chunk
  pivot_longer( # the code below here is similar to that from tidy-data
    cols = contains("year"),
    names_to = c("names", "year"),
    names_sep = "_",
    values_to = "values",
    values_transform = list(values = as.character)
  ) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = names,
    values_from = values
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    year = parse_number(year),
    score = as.numeric(score),
    date = as.Date(date),
    across(c(sex:frl), ~str_to_lower(.))
  )


```

### Part 2

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### 1. Tidy the *Project Reads* data

-   Load the **Project_Reads_Scores.csv** file
-   Remove columns 5-9, 24, and 25
-   Filter to remove the rows in *student_id* that represent aggregate summaries
-   Tidy the remaining dataset such that a case represents a score and percentage within a unit (i.e., *score* and *percentage* will be separate columns). Take a VERY close look at the data. You will be able to use the `names_sep` argument if you **first** `rename()` two columns. Identify those two columns first. Also, you will need to first `pivot_longer` and then `pivot_wider` in order to tidy properly. In these data, "tidy" is a row for each of the seven *units* for every *student_id*.

```{r}
#| label: q1
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(janitor)
library(ggthemes)

theme_set(theme_minimal())

reads <- read_csv(here("data", "Project_Reads_Scores.csv")) %>% 
  clean_names()


reads_tidy <- reads %>% 
  select(4, 1:3, 10:23) %>% 
  rename("unit_56_score" = "unit_5_6_score", 
         "unit_56_percent" = "unit_5_6_percent") %>% 
  filter(student_id != "All Students (Average)") %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = contains("unit"),
    names_prefix = "unit_",
    names_sep = "_",
    names_to = c("unit", "score_type"),
    values_to = "score",
    values_transform = list(score = as.character)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(score = parse_number(score)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = score_type,
    values_from = score
  )
```

#### 2. Produce a summary table of the mean percentage correct for each unit within test sites. Report the summary in a table.

```{r}
#| label: q2
#| output: false

reads_summary <- reads_tidy %>% 
	group_by(test_site, unit) %>% 
	summarize(percent = mean(percent))

reads_summary %>% 
  kable()
```
